core_aesthetic_takeaways: This batch is strongest as a civic-cultural identity system reference rather than a single poster style.
The transferable visual DNA is a modular circular C-like symbol language, not the exact logo itself.
The palette is highly distinctive: cream, oxblood brown, cyan, orange-red, pale yellow, soft gray, and dark brown type.
The best training value is cross-application consistency across posters, signage, stationery, outdoor media, facade signage, apparel, and social posts.
The batch helps solve fragmented visuals by showing how one small symbol grammar can expand into many touchpoints while staying ordered.
prompt_structure_lessons: Start prompts by naming the application type: poster, wayfinding signage, stationery, facade sign, social grid, or brand guideline board.
Describe the identity grammar separately from the layout: circular modular marks, notch/arrow cutouts, three accent colors, cream/brown fields.
Lock object count and medium before adding cultural references; otherwise social posts, signage arrows, and architecture can collapse into one cluttered scene.
For text, specify exact short headlines only and mark small multilingual copy as placeholder unless source text is supplied.
When using architectural signage, preserve facade perspective and keep the logo lockup integrated into the surface.

text_accuracy_policy.training_rule: Use this batch for hierarchy, grid rhythm, color coding, signage logic, and application consistency.

risk_controls.mitigation: Caption the mark as modular circular civic-symbol grammar; avoid using the exact mark as a reusable generated brand asset unless the user explicitly requests this project identity.
Only train short verified headlines as exact text; treat small Italian, English, Chinese, address, email, and pinyin-like details as placeholder layout.
Keep separate view_type labels for poster, signage, stationery, facade, social media, apparel, and color-system boards.
Downweight the low-resolution facade image and use the high-resolution version as the primary facade signage reference.
Treat the Instagram-like chrome as presentation context, not a required brand element.
Use cultural imagery only inside specific event posts; keep the core identity geometric and restrained.

recommended_training_use.stage_1_curation: include as a high-quality VI and public-signage identity batch after rights review
recommended_training_use.stage_2_caption_tuning: use captions to teach modular identity grammar, application separation, and multilingual text-risk control
recommended_training_use.stage_3_lora_training: train as a VI/signage adapter with additional public cultural-institution identity cases before mixing with packaging or product photography

negative_prompt_atoms: random floating circles without grid logic
lanterns, dragons, and generic cultural ornaments unless requested
social media UI chrome in every output
context_routing_rule: Treat this batch as civic cultural identity and public cultural communication. It can inform Culture China systems, but it is not a retail conversion project.
